stage: encrypted local storage primitive; not yet wired to send/restore/recovery lifecycle
changes: Added pendingGroupSendStorage with AES-256-GCM sealed manifests and separately sealed original/transmitted files. Content, remote payload, file keys, names, MIME types and timestamps are inside authenticated envelopes. AAD binds account, device, group, request and manifest/file role/index; fresh 96-bit IVs are used per part.

Reuses the existing mqvi_e2ee metadata store under exact JSON-scoped v1 namespaces; no new database, dependency or schema migration. Non-exportable local CryptoKeys are created under a read-write transaction so concurrent tabs cannot overwrite each other's key. Missing keys with existing records fail closed rather than regenerating and orphaning data.

Pending records are write-once per operation key; conflicting writes are rejected. Context guards surround asynchronous crypto/file/IDB steps. Failed/stale writes are surfaced, not reported as durable success. Conditional cleanup uses a unique write token so it cannot remove a replacement record.

Restore validates scope, payload/device/request identity, key algorithm, file-count/descriptor/key metadata and authenticated file sizes. Corrupt/tampered records are reported by scope without automatic deletion. Exact-key removal and existing logout metadata cleanup cover records and keys.

Existing portable backup collection does not include these local metadata namespaces. Existing local restore rollback snapshots the metadata store, preserving non-exportable pending keys and sealed records on failed restore. Storage comments now correctly disclose that older identity/session/message-cache records remain unencrypted by this wrapper and do not assume OS full-disk encryption is enabled.
Initial tests exposed a genuine cross-realm ArrayBuffer rejection; validation now uses the native brand-checking byteLength getter rather than instanceof or spoofable toString tags.
verification: Real WebCrypto plus fake-indexeddb tests verify connection close/reopen restore of exact original/transmitted bytes and metadata, non-exportable keys, no plaintext strings in raw record structure, owner/device separation, AAD group/part swaps rejected, six concurrent key creators interoperating, write-once behavior, missing-key failure and logout clearing.

Context cancellation and injected QuotaExceededError propagate without a pending record. This is injected storage failure, not a real disk-full browser test. Malformed snapshots fail before key/record creation.

Three crypto suites passed: 65 tests (pending storage, keyStorage, keyBackup). Added backup rollback test confirms the original local CryptoKey can still decrypt its sealed record after a failed restore; the backup layer is mocked metadata storage while crypto is real.

Full client regression passed before the last validation/test follow-up: 225 files / 2146 tests in 46.03s. Final seven pending-storage tests passed afterward (1.58s). Final tsc -b, targeted ESLint and git diff --check passed; an initial preserve-caught-error lint failure was fixed by attaching the caught cause.

Local Vite web production build passed: 1648 modules, 706ms; existing warnings remain unsuppressed. The storage module is not yet imported by the send runtime, so the unchanged module count/build does not prove live persistence or restart recovery.
remaining: Wire write-before-first-POST, authenticated startup restore, ready-device/account/group affinity, multi-operation ordering, encrypted cleanup and persistent partial-file recovery. Do not mark runtime pending sends durable yet; UI still correctly warns session-only retention.

Preserve unresolved partial uploads across subsequent sends and restart rather than deleting their snapshot too early or overwriting one group slot. Handle cancellation/completion deletion failure and newer draft reconciliation explicitly.

Real browser/Electron process restart, actual storage quota failure, large-file memory/quota pressure, cross-tab lifecycle/logout races and successful backup/device-reset user warnings remain unverified. Backup rollback snapshots may become large with pending file ciphertext and need proportionate acceptance.
Non-exportable IndexedDB keys do not protect against compromised same-origin scripts. Existing plaintext message-cache/session storage was not converted to encrypted at-rest storage by this change.
No actual two-client/Windows acceptance, production update, commit, push, merge or release performed. Overall P0-P11 remains incomplete.
